## Fixed

- **`saved-queries` ran the wrong window when a timezone was set.** The window was formatted in UTC but sent with the configured zone, so with `Asia/Kolkata` the server read the bounds 5h30m early. Saved queries now format and label the window in the same zone, like `collections` already did. `find` also sends the resolved zone.
- **Invalid timezones are rejected.** `logchef config set timezone` accepts only IANA zone names such as `Asia/Kolkata` or `UTC

**The OpenCode plugin works with OpenCode 2.x.** OpenCode 2.x dropped the 1.x plugin API, so the plugin `cymbal hook install opencode` wrote had no effect there: no reminder, no nudge. The installer now writes one plugin that serves both: OpenCode 1.x runs it as before, and 2.x adds cymbal's reminder to the system prompt before each model request and nudges code searches run through its shell tool. On 2.x, Grep and Glob calls are not nudged, because 2.x tool hooks can only change a tool's input. The path, t

**Empty results are results.** `impact` on a symbol nothing calls used to fail with "no callers found", the same thing it printed for a name that doesn't exist. Now it exits 0 with its usual header and `total_callers: 0`, or an empty `results` list in `--json`. `trace`, `refs` and `refs --importers` do the same when they have nothing to show, and `trace --json` prints JSON instead of a plain-text note. A name the index has never seen exits 1 with `symbol not found: X` in all four commands, as in `show` and

**Fixed** path filters being applied after result limits, which could hide a match just past the cutoff; `trace` dropping real one- and two-letter callees like `Do`; and `--db ./custom.db` changing the permissions of the folder it lives in.

- **`index --force <subdir>` wrote to an orphaned DB** — the DB path was hashed from the subdirectory instead of the git root, so the indexed data was invisible to every query command, and a scoped walk could prune files outside the subtree. Indexing now resolves the git root (via `EvalSymlinks` first, so a symlink into a subtree also lands in the right DB), walks and prunes only within the scope, and keeps `rel_path` repo-relative. See the [migration instructions](https://github.com/fcoury/oxide/blob/v0.2.0/docs/compatibility.md#storage-version-and-legacy-databases).

## Highlights

### Start your first lesson while your plan is still being built

When you set up a new subject, we now start writing your course while you answer the setup questions, and you can begin lesson 1 as soon as it's ready instead of waiting for the whole plan. A short quiz keeps you busy in the meantime, with progress shown in a small line on your phone or beside the quiz on a bigger screen. Whichever is ready first, lesson 1 or your plan, is the one we offer. When you finish lesson 1, **See your

If a save fails twice in a row, the "Still not going through" line now has a **Report a problem** link under it. It opens the feedback form with "I couldn't save my answers." already filled in, so sending takes one more tap. You can do this on placement, the level test, practice, checkpoints, mistakes, essays, pronunciation and lesson ends. Guests can send it too, with an email if they'd like a reply. The report goes through a separate route from your answers, so it can reach us even when your saves can't.

## Highlights

### A language certificate now means you finished the level

You now earn a language certificate by finishing that level in your plan and studying at least half of its lessons. Under the old rules, a level test and a few good answers could be enough: one learner placed at B1+ got a B1 certificate after 2 lessons and 8 minutes. Each language now has six certificates, from A1 to C2. The Level card on Today and Progress follows your plan as well, and unit pages show the exact level of their less
- After a missed answer from "I can't talk now", the feedback now shows the right translation, like a regular listening screen does. (#2398)

Calls now start when you're ready. An intro explains how they work, and you tap to call. The transcript follows along, a bar shows whose turn it is, and the character starts talking in about 1.5 seconds, down from 2.4. Calls end with a goodbye at a natural pause, where they used to cut off mid-sentence, and a daily limit never cuts a call short. If a call drops, "Call again" picks it up where it stopped, and your feedback covers the whole conversation. (#1924, #1956)
